name: The Hollow Crown of Aldric

relationships.label: The Hollow Crown of Aldric was cursed by Mourne the Hollow King — the soul pact that Aldric swore bound the crown itself to Mourne's will, and whoever wears it hears his voice forever.
The Hollow Crown was forged in Greyvast and worn by its last king — it is the crown of a dead city, and it carries the weight of every soul lost in its fall.
The Oathbound Remnants search for the Hollow Crown, believing that retrieving it is the first step toward breaking the soul pact and freeing Greyvast's dead from Mourne's claim.
The Hollow Crown was created during the Fall of Greyvast — Aldric wore it when he made his pact with Mourne, and the crown was lost in the chaos that followed.

description: The Hollow Crown of Aldric is a cursed relic from Greyvast's final hour. Worn by King Aldric when he made the soul pact with Mourne the Hollow King — trading the souls of Greyvast's dead for a brief moment of mercy — the crown now carries Mourne's voice within it. Anyone who wears it hears the Hollow King speaking, always, and the longer they wear it, the more they forget of themselves. The Oathbound Remnants search for it. The Pale Dominion wants it destroyed. Both agree it should never be worn again.
excerpt: The cursed crown of Greyvast's last king — wear it and hear Mourne's voice. The Remnants search for it. The Dominion wants it destroyed.
content:
The Hollow Crown of Aldric is not a beautiful thing. It is iron, blackened, seven uneven points rising from a band that has never fit any head comfortably. The iron is pitted, scarred, as if it has been through fire and water and worse. The inside of the band is inscribed with words so small and so old that no living scholar has read them — but those who have worn the crown report that the words are not meant to be read with the eyes.

King Aldric put the crown on during the Fall of Greyvast. The city was drowning — literally drowning, the mist rising from the coast like a tide that would not stop, and with it the Hollowed, the Grief-Echoes, the slow corruption of everything the city had been. Aldric had no army. He had no allies. He had only the crown, and the mist, and a god who was listening. He made the pact on his knees in the throne room, seawater at his waist, the crown cold against his brow. Mourne accepted. Greyvast fell anyway.

The crown was lost in the evacuation. Some say it sank with the throne room. Some say a Tide-Weaver salvaged it and sold it south, where it passed through hands that did not know what they were holding. The Oathbound Remnants have been searching for it since the day Greyvast fell. They believe that if they can find the crown, they can study the pact — perhaps break it, perhaps release the souls Mourne claimed. The Pale Dominion has a different view. They believe the crown is a trap, that Mourne put his voice in it deliberately, and that wearing it is the fastest path to becoming a Pale-Touched. Both sides are probably right.

Three known people have worn the crown since Aldric. The first was a Tide-Weaver diver who found it in a submerged armory. He surfaced, put it on, and did not speak again for three days. When he finally spoke, he recited the names of Greyvast's dead in order, without pause, for seven hours. He died that night, his soul fully eroded. The second was an Arch-Seer of the Pale Dominion who believed she could purify it. She lasted two weeks. The third — a Greyvasti elder who refused to give up the search — wore it for less than an hour before removing it, her eyes silver-white. She has not spoken since. She writes, when she writes at all, in a language no one recognizes. The crown sits in a locked box in Mournwall, waiting for someone foolish enough to try again.

name: A Moon Fragment (Grade 3)

relationships.label: Every moon fragment in Northern Velkaris originates from the Celestial Fracture — the shattering of the moon scattered millions of pieces across the region, and Grade 3 is the most common size.
Grade 3 moon fragments are the primary trade commodity of the Tide-Weavers — they salvage, grade, and sell them across Northern Velkaris as the region's only reliable currency.
The Pale Dominion venerates moon fragments as Yssara's living body — Grade 3 fragments are used in daily rites, distributed to the faithful, and consumed in the Ritual of Controlled Erosion.
All moon fragments attract the Hollowed — Grade 3 fragments draw them from miles away, making salvage operations a constant race against the approaching drift of empty bodies.

description: A Grade 3 moon fragment — the standard mid-sized shard produced by the Celestial Fracture. Roughly the size of a fist, faintly luminous, warm to the touch. It is simultaneously the region's primary currency, its most powerful magical fuel, its most sacred sacrament, and a slow poison that erodes the soul of anyone who carries it too long. The Tide-Weavers trade them. The Pale Dominion prays with them. The Hollowed walk toward them. Everyone in Northern Velkaris has held one. Everyone will eventually be damaged by one.
excerpt: The most common moon fragment — currency, sacrament, weapon, and poison. Everyone in Northern Velkaris has held one. Everyone will be damaged by one.
content:
A Grade 3 moon fragment fits in the palm of your hand. It is roughly the size and weight of a fist, its surface smooth to the touch where it was once jagged — the edges have been worn down by handling, by water, by the slow pressure of being passed from hand to hand. It is warm, always, as if recently held, even when it has been sitting in a crate for weeks. In darkness, it glows. A faint, steady silver-blue light that illuminates the veins in your fingers when you hold it up.

The Tide-Weavers grade fragments by size and purity. Grade 1 is dust. Grade 2 is a fingernail clipping. Grade 3 is the standard — the size of a fist, pure enough to power a minor ritual or fuel a lamp for a month, small enough to carry in a pocket. A Grade 3 fragment will buy you a room in Ashenveil for a week, or a passage south, or a weapon, or a hour of an Arch-Seer's time. It is the closest thing Northern Velkaris has to coin.

The cost of handling a Grade 3 fragment is measurable. Every hour of unprotected contact accelerates soul erosion. The Tide-Weavers have developed tools for safe handling — lead-lined gloves, crystal tongs, storage boxes of treated stone — but the safeguards are expensive, and not everyone can afford them. The refugees of Ashenveil carry fragments in their bare hands because they have no choice. The Dominion distributes fragments to the faithful as a test of faith — those who can endure the erosion are closer to Yssara. The children of Greyvast survivors were born clutching fragments, and their eyes are silver, and they will be dead by forty.

The Hollowed sense fragments. A Grade 3 fragment carried openly will draw every Hollowed within a mile toward the carrier. The Tide-Weavers have learned to navigate this — they move fragments in sealed stone containers, at night, through routes that avoid known drift-patterns. But the risk is never zero. Every fragment is a beacon. Every carrier is a target. And yet the trade continues because the alternative — a Northern Velkaris without moon fragments — is a Northern Velkaris without magic, without currency, without heat, without light. The fragments are killing them. They cannot survive without them.

name: The Erosion Codex

relationships.label: The Erosion Codex is the sacred text of the Doctrine of Controlled Erosion — it contains the theological and ritual foundation upon which the entire Dominion faith is built.
The Erosion Codex was authored by the first Arch-Seers of the Pale Dominion, transcribing the revelations of the First Moon Ritual into codified law and liturgy.
The Erosion Codex documents the First Moon Ritual in its entirety — it is the written record of what Yssara revealed to the First Voice, preserved through generations of Arch-Seers.
The Tide-Weavers stole one of the seven known copies of the Erosion Codex from a Dominion scriptorium — their reasons remain unclear, but the theft has not been acknowledged by either side.

description: The Erosion Codex is the sacred text of the Pale Dominion, written by the first Arch-Seers from the revelations of the First Moon Ritual. It contains the complete theology of the Doctrine of Controlled Erosion — instructions for soul sacrifice, fragment activation, the hierarchy of holy erosion, and the liturgical calendar. Seven copies are known to exist. One was stolen by the Tide-Weavers. The Dominion has not admitted the theft exists.
excerpt: The sacred text of the Pale Dominion — written in the blood of the first Arch-Seers. Seven copies exist. One was stolen by the Tide-Weavers.
content:
The Erosion Codex is not a book you read. It is a book you submit to.

Each of the seven known copies is bound in pale leather — human skin, the Arch-Seers do not deny this — stretched over boards made from the compressed bone of Greyvasti who died during the Fall. The pages are not paper. They are vellum, scraped thin from the skin of Pale-Touched who donated their bodies to the faith before reaching Stage Six. The ink is silver, ground from moon fragment dust mixed with the blood of the scribe who wrote the page. Every copy of the Codex contains traces of its own creation: the scribe's blood, the donor's skin, the bone of the dead.

The text is divided into seven sections, each attributed to one of the seven original Arch-Seers who witnessed the First Moon Ritual. The first section — The Doctrine of the Fragment — establishes Yssara as the divine source and the moon fragments as her living body. The second — The Hierarchy of Erosion — codifies the ranking system of the Dominion clergy based on how much of their soul they have sacrificed. The third — The Liturgy of Offering — contains the precise rituals for soul-sacrifice, including chants, postures, and the required purity grades of moon fragments for each ceremony.

The fourth section is the one the Tide-Weavers stole. It is titled The Catalog of Prohibited Applications, and it lists uses of moon fragments that the Dominion has declared heretical — uses that even the Arch-Seers consider too dangerous to permit. The Tide-Weavers have not revealed what they found in the stolen section, but their salvage operations have become more targeted, more secretive, and more successful since the theft. The Dominion has not acknowledged that a copy is missing. To admit the Codex can be stolen is to admit that Yssara's protection is not absolute.

Reading the Codex is itself an act of erosion. The silver ink radiates a low, constant dose of fragment energy — a full reading of all seven sections is estimated to cost the reader approximately three months of lifespan. The Arch-Seers consider this appropriate. Knowledge has a price, they say, and the knowledge of how to destroy yourself should cost something.

name: The Pact Shard

relationships.label: The Pact Shard was the moon fragment used in the First Moon Ritual — the First Voice held this specific stone when Yssara spoke, and it cracked the moment the ritual ended.
The Pact Shard is secretly held by the Tide-Weavers — they recovered it from a submerged scriptorium and immediately stopped selling their most lucrative fragments, drawing no attention.
The Pact Shard resonates with Yssara of the Shattered Moon at a frequency no other fragment matches — it vibrates when her name is spoken nearby, and its glow pulses in sync with the lunar cycle.

The Pale Dominion desperately seeks the Pact Shard, believing that recovering the original fragment of the First Moon Ritual would allow them to replicate Yssara's revelation and speak with her directly.

description: The Pact Shard is the specific moon fragment used in the First Moon Ritual — the stone the First Voice held when Yssara spoke for the first time. It is small, cracked down the middle, and still radiates more energy than fragments ten times its size. The Tide-Weavers recovered it from a submerged scriptorium and immediately stopped selling their most lucrative finds to avoid suspicion. It is the most important object in Northern Velkaris, and almost no one knows it exists.
excerpt: The original moon fragment from the First Moon Ritual — small, cracked, humming with impossible energy. The Tide-Weavers found it and told no one.
content:
It looks like nothing. That is the first thing anyone says when they see the Pact Shard. It is small — smaller than a Grade 3, closer to a Grade 2 in size. It fits in a closed fist with room to spare. A crack runs down its center, not quite clean, as if the stone was struck by something that did not have the force to break it but had every intention of trying.

And it hums.

The hum is not sound. It is vibration, felt in the bones of anyone within ten feet. The Tide-Weavers who recovered it described the sensation as standing near a low waterfall — a constant pressure, a presence that you stop noticing after a while, but that leaves you feeling hollow when you walk away. The shard resonates with Yssara. Speak her name in the same room, and the crack in the stone glows — a deep, pulsing silver that matches the rhythm of a heartbeat. The Tide-Weavers have learned not to speak her name near it.

The shard was found in a submerged scriptorium on the edge of the Sunken Quarter — a building that had collapsed into the water during Greyvast's fall and remained untouched for decades. The Tide-Weaver who found it was looking for Grade 4 fragments, not history. She brought up the shard in a standard salvage bag, logged it as Grade 2, and moved on. It was only when the quartermaster noticed that the stone would not stop glowing that anyone realized something was wrong.

The Tide-Weavers have kept the shard secret. They stopped selling their highest-grade fragments. They redirected salvage operations away from the scriptorium site. They told no one why. The Pale Dominion has heard rumors — they always hear rumors — but they do not know the shard exists. If they did, they would stop at nothing to recover it. The First Moon Ritual's original fragment, in the hands of a merchant guild that values profit over prophecy, is the kind of irony that the Arch-Seers would burn a city to correct.

The shard currently sits in a lead-lined box in a locked room in a building that does not officially exist, somewhere in the Tide-Weavers' quarter of the Sunken Quarter. The box has three locks. Two keys are held by Tide-Weaver captains who do not know what they are guarding. The third key does not exist — the lock was welded shut before the box was closed. If the shard is ever needed, the box will have to be cut open, and whoever cuts it open will feel the hum for the first time, and they will understand why the Tide-Weavers have not sold the most valuable object in Northern Velkaris. They are afraid of it.
